One floor, one door, one kettle

One long room, ten benches and a yard.

It was a joinery, then a tyre place, then empty for eleven years. The floor is still the original concrete and the rings on it are from the tyres, not from us.

The plan

  1. 1

    The long room

    Ten benches in two rows, each with a vice, a bench hook and a light you can swing. Two drop to seated height.

  2. 2

    Machine bay

    Bandsaw, planer thicknesser and a pillar drill, behind a partition, with extraction along the wall. Induction before you touch any of them.

  3. 3

    Timber store

    Offcuts free to members, boards priced on the shelf, and a rack of green wood under a wet sack.

  4. 4

    Kettle and sink

    The slowest kettle in the county, a sink deep enough for a bucket, and the only chair anybody fights over.

  5. 5

    Sharpening corner

    Stones, a strop and a grinder nobody is allowed to use in a hurry. Every edge in the building comes through here.

  6. 6

    The yard

    Chopping blocks, three stools, a table for the messy half of a class, and the willow that nobody planted.

Getting in

Level access from the yard through a door wide enough for a wheelchair, with no step at the threshold and no door closer to fight. The yard itself is flat and the gate is propped open on class nights.

The machine bay is loud enough that ear defenders are not optional. Two benches drop to seated height and one has a knee recess. Say what you need when you write and it will be set up before you arrive.

There is no parking. There is a bike rack that holds six, and it is bolted to something serious.
